title: NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own): Holding Several Building Policies
content:
**Rule.** A business, landlord, non-profit or condominium association may hold any number of General Property Form and RCBAP policies under the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own), one per insured building, or per non-residential condominium unit; there is no per-customer cap. Each building is a separate policy with its own limits, deductibles, premium and term, even when several buildings share one street address or one owner, and nothing on one policy is pooled into or offset against another policy of the same customer. A condominium association insures its buildings only under the RCBAP tiers, and an individual unit owner's interest is never written on this category.

## Points of judgement

| Question | Answer under the rule |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of policies one customer may hold? | No — the number per customer is uncapped (no figure is set). |
| Do two buildings at one street address share a limit or a deductible? | No — each building is its own policy with its own limits, deductibles, premium and term. |
| Can a credit or balance on one policy be applied to another policy of the same customer? | No — nothing on one policy is pooled into or offset against another. |
| Under which tiers does an association insure its buildings? | Only the RCBAP tiers. |
| Can an individual condominium unit owner's interest be written on this line? | Never. |

**Hypothetical holding.** A landlord owning three apartment buildings, two of them on the same street address, holds three separate policies: each has its own premium account and term, and a payment made on one is never moved to the others.
